description: The Froth is invisible and unmistakable: seventy-four thousand kilometers of vacuum that boils, its boundaries swelling and fraying like sea foam over a rising tide. Where the foam crests, starlight shivers and instruments report particles that decay too fast to exist. There is nothing to see and everything to detect.

Surges roll through the region on an irregular rhythm averaging nineteen hours, each one a fresh argument between matter and probability. Hulls crossing the froth exchange atoms with might-have-been; gauges read confidently and wrongly; once inside, crews learn that effects can precede their causes by whole minutes. The probe Candor-7 returned from a surge still transmitting a thorough proof of its own non-existence.

Cosmologists date the froth to the universe's first billion years, a patch where spacetime never quite finished deciding to be smooth. It has resisted eleven decades of instrumentation, three unified theories, and one very expensive containment buoy now believed to be distributed across several outcomes. Energy consortium watch its surges the way prospectors watch rivers.

Drones map it constantly and disagree constantly, which researchers insist is the data. Harvest rigs skim the boundary during calm intervals, siphoning fluctuation energy that powers small colonies. Entry remains legal, insured against acts of physics, and discouraged by everyone who has come back.
